steps: Eagles are parrots, parrots are birds so some birds are eagles: II follows
III: all birds are crows not implied
Option C wrong: III does not follow, so not an either-or pair; A,B include false I
check_code:
import itertools
# universe of 4 types: bits for (crow,eagle,parrot,bird) membership; enumerate models with nonempty sets
types=[t for t in itertools.product([0,1],repeat=4)]
def valid(t):
    c,e,p,b=t
    return (not c or p) and (not e or p) and (not p or b)
vt=[t for t in types if valid(t)]
res=[True,True,True]
for r in range(1,len(vt)+1):
    for m in itertools.combinations(vt,r):
        if not all(any(t[i] for t in m) for i in range(4)): continue
        I=not any(t[0] and t[3] for t in m)
        II=any(t[3] and t[1] for t in m)
        III=all(t[0] for t in m if t[3])
        res[0]&=I;res[1]&=II;res[2]&=III
assert res==[False,True,False]
opts={'A':(1,1,1),'B':(1,0,1),'C':None,'D':(0,1,0)}
follow=tuple(int(x) for x in res)
assert follow==opts['D']
assert follow!=opts['A'] and follow!=opts['B']
# C: either II or III requires exactly one; II follows alone but reading 'either..or' as II or III (III false) not the exact statement

check_code:
import itertools
types=list(itertools.product([0,1],repeat=4))  # pea,carrot,veg,green
vt=[t for t in types if (not t[0] or t[2]) and (not t[1] or t[2]) and (not t[2] or t[3])]
res=[True]*3
for r in range(1,len(vt)+1):
    for m in itertools.combinations(vt,r):
        if not all(any(t[i] for t in m) for i in range(4)): continue
        res[0]&=all(t[3] for t in m if t[0])
        res[1]&=all(t[1] for t in m if t[3])
        res[2]&=any(t[3] and t[0] for t in m)
assert res==[True,False,True]
S={i+1 for i,x in enumerate(res) if x}
opts={'A':{2,3},'B':{1,2,3},'C':{1,3},'D':{1,2}}
assert S==opts['C']
assert all(S!=v for k,v in opts.items() if k!='C')
